title: "Instructor notes"

## Before the workshop

| When | Task |
|---|---|
| 3–4 weeks before | Send the pre-workshop survey (below) and the [Setup](setup.qmd) page |
| 2 weeks before | Group participants by experience; decide on Python/R split and Day 2 tracks |
| 1 week before | Optional 60-minute online session: Colab basics, run Lab 02 together |
| 2–3 days before | **Run every lab in Colab, in both languages** — especially 7A and 7C, which rely on external services |
| Day before | Download a copy of the `data/` folder to a USB stick in case of Wi-Fi problems |

**Pre-workshop survey (5 questions)**

1. Field: crop science, animal science, plant biology, microbiology, ecology, molecular biology, other
2. Coding experience: none / some R / some Python / comfortable
3. Data types you work with: field trials, sensors/drones, images, sequences, genotypes, omics, other
4. One problem you hope AI could help with
5. Have you used ChatGPT, Claude or similar tools for work?

## During the workshop

- **Helpers:** one per 8 participants, ideally covering both Python and R.
- **Stuck / done signal:** coloured sticky notes on laptops (red = stuck, green = done).
- **Live coding:** type slowly, narrate, and make (and fix) mistakes on purpose.
- **Pair programming** works well for mixed groups: one Python and one R user can compare results — they should match.
- **Muddiest point cards** at the end of Day 1; answer them first thing on Day 2.
- **No-code fallback:** [Orange Data Mining](https://orangedatamining.com) reproduces Labs 03–05 with drag and drop for anyone who struggles with code.

## Lab timing guide

| Lab | Core (must do) | Optional | Typical time |
|---|---|---|---|
| 02 | Part A, Part C | Part B (or B instead of C for geneticists) | 45 min |
| 03 | Part A, one of B/C | the other of B/C | 60 min |
| 04 | Part A leakage, Part C batch | overfitting curve, Part B, selection leakage | 50 min |
| 05 | Part B or C | Part A | 40 min |
| 06 | Sections 1, 3 | 2, 4 | 30 min |
| 07 | one track | — | 80 min |
| 08 | Functions 1–3 | Function 4, extra exercises | 40 min |

## After the workshop

- Share the site link, slides and a feedback survey with pre/post confidence ratings (1–5) for each learning outcome.
- Set up a shared channel or mailing list for one to two months.
- Offer an online clinic 4–6 weeks later where participants bring progress on their own data or capstone plans.

## Maintaining this site

### How it is built

```
labs/python/*.py, labs/r/*.R      ← the single source of every lab (edit these)
        │  python tools/build_labs.py
        ├── notebooks/{python,r}/*.ipynb   Colab notebooks (no outputs)
        └── _labs/*.md + figures/labs/     executed outputs, included in the pages
modules/*.qmd                      ← lecture notes; each includes its lab
data/simulate_data.py              ← regenerates every dataset
```

The lab scripts use `# %%` cell markers, so they also run cell by cell in RStudio, Positron, VS Code or Spyder.

### Rebuilding after editing a lab

You need Python with `requirements.txt`, R with `install.R`, and the R Jupyter kernel (`IRkernel::installspec()` in R).

```bash
python tools/build_labs.py              # all labs (about 4 minutes)
python tools/build_labs.py --only 04    # just Lab 04
python tools/build_labs.py --no-execute # notebooks only, no outputs
quarto preview                          # view the site locally
```

Labs 7A and 7C are not executed during the build (they need a GPU and internet), so their pages show code without outputs.

Commit the regenerated `notebooks/`, `_labs/` and `figures/` folders. GitHub Actions then renders and publishes the site; it does not need Python or R.

### Using your own GitHub account

The Colab buttons and data links point to `abu85/ai-for-agri-bio`. After creating your repository, run once:

```bash
python tools/set_repo.py your-username/your-repo-name
```

and commit the changes.
